# [CS016] Debug Endpoint Exposed (debug-endpoint-exposed)

pprof or expvar handlers are served on the public listener.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-489](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/489.html) |
| **OWASP** | A02:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Importing net/http/pprof registers profiling handlers on http.DefaultServeMux. On a public server they disclose memory contents, goroutine stacks and command-line flags and allow expensive profiling requests.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
import _ "net/http/pprof"

func main() { http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil) }
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
func main() {
	go func() { _ = http.ListenAndServe("127.0.0.1:6060", nil) }() // pprof on loopback only
	_ = http.ListenAndServe(":8080", appMux)
}
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [debug-endpoint-exposed]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    debug-endpoint-exposed: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore debug-endpoint-exposed -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** debug-endpoint-exposed
```
